_comment: Distinguishing levers for style families that would otherwise converge into near-identical cards. gen-briefs.ts inlines the value for your style into your brief. Where a style is absent, it has no twin — just render it faithfully.
minimalism-and-swiss-style: You are the 1950s Swiss original: strict visible 12-column grid, zero ornament, no shadows, no gradients, geometric sans-serif, generous whitespace, one accent colour used sparingly. Your twin swiss-modernism-2-0 is YOU but looser — if it looks exactly like you, one of you is wrong.
swiss-modernism-2-0: Swiss discipline with a modern loosening: keep the grid and the restraint, but use ONE oversized expressive headline and much more dramatic scale contrast than classic minimalism allows. Distinct from minimalism-and-swiss-style by that single act of typographic excess.
exaggerated-minimalism: Not grid-minimalism. Your move is one enormous element and very little else — a huge number, one giant word, or one oversized photo dominating an almost empty viewport. Tiny supporting text. Whitespace is the composition, not the padding.
minimal-and-direct: A conversion-first landing style, not an art movement: minimal because it removes everything that does not sell. Single column, no nav, no decoration, one clear action above the fold, short copy blocks. It should feel like a funnel, not a gallery.
flat-design: No depth at all: no shadows, no gradients, no blur, no bevels. Bold flat colour blocks, hard edges, illustrated-feeling shapes. Distinguished from every minimal style by COLOUR confidence — yours is saturated and chunky, theirs is quiet and neutral.
brutalism: Raw and deliberately unfinished: default-looking system fonts, visible unstyled structure, harsh black borders, no rounding, no polish, awkward overlaps left in on purpose. It should look like a 1996 page that knows what it is. Your twin neubrutalism is the commercialised, tidy version — if you look tidy, you are wrong.
neubrutalism: Brutalism made marketable: thick 3-4px black borders, HARD OFFSET SHADOWS (box-shadow: 8px 8px 0 #000, no blur), bright block colours, chunky rounded-free cards, playful rather than hostile. The offset shadow is the single giveaway that separates you from brutalism.
bento-box-grid: Fixed-span bento: an explicit grid where each cell has a deliberate size (2x1, 1x2, 2x2) forming a tidy mosaic, all cells flush to a regular track. Think Japanese bento box — compartments, ordered. Your twin bento-grids is the loose one.
bento-grids: Loose masonry bento: variable-height cards packed by flow rather than by a fixed track, with uneven bottoms and mixed scales. Where bento-box-grid is a mosaic, you are a corkboard. Do not align to a regular grid.
aurora-ui: Living aurora: ANIMATED, moving multi-stop gradient blobs drifting behind translucent content, with continuous motion (and a still state under reduced-motion). The movement is the style. gradient-mesh-aurora-evolved is your static sibling.
gradient-mesh-aurora-evolved: A still, printed gradient mesh — soft airbrushed colour transitions baked into surfaces, no animation, treated like a physical printed backdrop. Distinguished from aurora-ui by being motionless and by the mesh being part of the surface, not floating behind it.
neumorphism: Soft UI of the original school: one single consistent light source, elements extruded from or pressed into the SAME coloured background using paired light/dark shadows, low contrast, monochromatic, rounded 12-16px. No borders. soft-ui-evolution is the accessible descendant.
soft-ui-evolution: Neumorphism corrected for real use: keep the soft extruded look but ADD visible borders and raised contrast so boundaries never depend on a shadow alone, and mix it onto a proper surface palette rather than one monotone. Your difference is legibility, not a new shape language.
claymorphism: Playdough, not plaster: puffy inflated 3D-looking shapes, thick soft rounded corners (24px+), pastel colours, inner shadows making solid pillow volume, toy-like and warm. Softer and rounder than either neumorphism style, and distinctly colourful.
glassmorphism: Frosted panels floating over a vibrant, busy background — backdrop-filter blur 10-20px, translucent white fills at 10-30%, 1px hairline light borders, visible depth layering. The background MUST be interesting through the glass or you are just grey cards.
spatial-ui-visionos: Glass and depth in a spatial-computing sense: layered translucent panes at different z-distances, content that appears to float off the surface with parallax on pointer, strong rounded rectangles, thin bright edge highlights. Distinguished from glassmorphism by DEPTH STAGING — several discrete planes, not one frosted sheet.
dimensional-layering: Depth through stacking of opaque layers: overlapping flat planes with real z-order, cast shadows between strata, cards deliberately tucked behind one another. Not glass, not soft UI — you are paper cut-outs in a box, and the layering is the subject.
organic-biophilic: A living room: plants, natural materials, greens and earth tones, leaf shapes, organic curved section dividers, daylight softness. Biophilic = nature brought INTO the interface.
biomimetic-organic-2-0: Nature as a SYSTEM rather than decoration: growth-inspired layouts, cell/venicle/nest structures, forms that appear to have evolved, muted mineral palette, asymmetric clustering. Distinguished from organic-biophilic by being structural and afield-of-shapes rather than botanical imagery.
nature-distilled: Nature REDUCED to an essence: a restrained palette taken from landscape (fog, stone, lichen), subtle textures, calm gradients, almost no literal imagery. You are the quietest of the three nature styles — a mood, not a botanical.
accessible-and-ethical: Accessibility AS the design language: very high contrast, large type, obvious focus rings, generous hit areas, clear reading rhythm, honest plain language, no motion that is not meaningful. Visible affordance everywhere.
inclusive-design: Adaptable rather than merely compliant: multiple ways to see the same content, controls for text size and contrast shown IN the interface as design features, mixed-ability representation, forgiving layouts. The difference: accessible-and-ethical hides its accommodations, you display them.
motion-driven: The page is the animation: scroll-choreographed sequences, timed reveals that carry the narrative, large transforms and motion as the primary expressive device. Motion is the content.
micro-interactions: Motion at small scale: the page itself is calm, but every hover, press, toggle, field focus and checkbox has a carefully tuned response. Your quality shows in 120ms details, not in big scroll events.
kinetic-typography: Type itself moves and is the primary visual: letterforms animate, headline text is the hero image, weight/scale/spacing in motion. You have permission to split headline text into per-letter spans — declare it via the escape hatch, keep every data-tid string intact.
parallax-storytelling: Layered scroll narrative: fixed/sticky layers moving at different rates, chapters unfolding down the page, deep background vs near foreground. Distinguished from motion-driven by LAYERED DEPTH at differing scroll speeds rather than choreographed timing.
retro-futurism: The future as imagined in the 1970s-80s: chrome, sunsets in banded gradients, CRT glow, warm amber and magenta, wide-set type, optimistic space-age geometry. Retro-futurism is hopeful.
vaporwave: A specific nostalgic aesthetic: purple-to-pink gradients, teal, Greek/roman numerals, grid horizons, glitch and scanline, low saturation statuary. Ironic and hazy, where retro-futurism is sincere.
y2k-aesthetic: The year 2000 futurism: chrome and holographic surfaces, bubblegum pinks and cyans, blob shapes, starburst motifs, translucent plastics, tech optimism with a mall texture.
cyberpunk-ui: Night city: black base, neon cyan/magenta, terminal and HUD fragments, heavy glow, rain-slick gradients, monospaced data, dense overlaid metadata. Not recommended for light mode — still implement it, just keep it recognisable.
hud-sci-fi-fui: A functional Heads-Up Display: thin precise strokes, corner brackets, tick marks, monospaced telemetry, crosshairs, data readouts, translucent panels over dark. FUI is engineered and information-dense; cyberpunk is atmospheric and decorative.
pixel-art: Everything snapped to a coarse pixel grid: image-rendering: pixelated on photos, hard-edged blocky borders, 8-bit colour discipline, chunky sprite-like icons and buttons, no anti-aliasing, no smooth gradients.
gen-z-chaos-maximalism: Deliberate visual chaos: clashing colours, overlapping stickers, rotated elements, doodles, mixed fonts, internet-native collage. Density is the point. anti-polish is quieter and more sincere.
anti-polish-raw-aesthetic: Handmade and unrefined rather than chaotic: visible editing marks, default form controls, unaligned elements, mismatched type, photocopy textures. Sincereal roughness, a zine — not a meme.
memphis-design: 1980s Memphis Group specifically: squiggles, zigzags and triangles as confetti shapes, black-and-white patterned fills beside saturated primaries, thin outlines, playful geometry on a light base.
vibrant-and-block-based: Big saturated colour blocks as the organising structure: heavy solid rectangles of clashing vivid hue, thick type, high energy, deliberate poster composition. Colour BLOCKS, not gradients or shapes.
editorial-grid-magazine: A print magazine: multi-column body text, drop caps, rules and hairlines, folio numbers, pull quotes, asymmetric editorial spreads, serif-led hierarchy. Typographic and dense in an orderly way.
chromatic-aberration-rgb-split: The lens error IS the style: red/cyan offset fringes on text and edges, colour-channel ghosting, slight blur at extremes, high contrast against dark. Everything looks photographed through imperfect glass.
vintage-analog-retro-film: Photographic ageing: film grain, faded warm palette, halation, light leaks, soft vignettes, printed-paper texture, slight blur. The imagery is degraded; the layout can be clean.
e-ink-paper: A reading device: paper white background, near-black ink, no glow, no shadow, no gradient, high x-height serif, generous leading, flat matte surfaces. Not recommended for dark mode — implement it anyway as a 'night paper' interpretation.
dark-mode-oled: True black (#000) surfaces with luminous content, minimal glow, no gradients on the background, colour used only as signal. Light mode is still required — make it a deliberate 'daylight OLED' interpretation rather than skipping it.
skeuomorphism: Literal material imitation: the UI objects look like their physical referents — stitched leather, brushed metal, wood, glossy buttons with specular highlights, real shadows under real objects. Commits to the illusion.
3d-and-hyperrealism: Depth with rendered realism: volumetric forms, dramatic lighting, photographic composite imagery, heavy blur/DOF, rich shadows. Distinguished from skeuomorphism by being a rendered scene rather than an imitated object.
3d-product-preview: An interactive 3-D viewport is the centrepiece: a canvas host you can rotate, with control affordances around it. You have permission to add a canvas via the escape hatch; keep the canonical booking controls reachable.
tactile-digital-deformable-ui: Interfaces that physically yield: elements squash, bend and deform under the pointer, springy press states, rubbery geometry. Input has consequences on the shape of things.
interactive-cursor-design: The pointer is the interface: custom cursor replacing the native one, trailing particles or shape, elements reacting to proximity and cursor position. Add your cursor node via the escape hatch and declare it; keep native controls usable.
voice-first-multimodal: Voice as the primary channel with screen as fallback: a visible listening state, waveform, suggested utterances, and a clearly offered manual path. Add mic affordances via the escape hatch; the canonical booking form must remain fully usable.
ai-native-ui: An AI product's visual grammar: streaming/generative reveals, suggestion chips, confidence indicators, prompt-like inputs, subtle gradient shimmer while 'thinking', conversational framing.
zero-interface: Progressive disclosure taken to the limit: almost nothing visible until summoned, intent-driven reveal on hover/focus/scroll, hidden controls appearing on demand. Declared deviation permitted — but every data-tid string must still exist and be reachable, never deleted.
hero-centric-design: Landing archetype — one overwhelming full-viewport hero carries the page; everything after is subordinate and sparse. Your distinguishing trait is the SIZE and dominance of the opening.
conversion-optimized: Landing archetype — every section exists to move toward one action: repeated CTAs, benefit-led headings, urgency and value framing, minimal exit points. Judge yourself on how hard it sells, not how pretty.
feature-rich-showcase: Landing archetype — breadth is the message: many features shown explicitly and completely, tabs or grids of capability, dense supporting detail, generous comparison tables.
social-proof-focused: Landing archetype — evidence from others leads: reviews, logos, ratings, traveller counts and results placed above and repeated; the itinerary supports the proof rather than the reverse.
trust-and-authority: Landing archetype — institutional credibility: conservative palette, precise typography, credentials, licences, guarantees, safety and policy language, formal tone. Restrained and assured.
storytelling-driven: Landing archetype — a narrative arc: the seven days told as a journey with a beginning, turn and resolution, first-person voice, scene-setting, sequential reveals.
interactive-product-demo: Landing archetype — show the thing working: controls the visitor can operate, live state changes, before/after and pick-a-day interactions that let them configure the trip.
